facts.statement: The fossil remains of Kayentasuchus were discovered in 1983 by paleontologist James M. Clark.
facts.quote: It was found in 1983 by James M. Clark.

facts.statement: The specimen was found at Willow Springs, located 50 kilometers northeast of Flagstaff.
facts.quote: The location was at Willow Springs, 50 km northeast of Flagstaff.

facts.statement: The skeleton was discovered in channel sandstone within the silty facies of the Kayenta Formation.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in a channel sandstone about halfway up the formation, in the "silty facies".

facts.statement: Fossils of the turtle Kayentachelys, the dinosaur Scutellosaurus, and tritylodonts were found nearby just meters below the Kayentasuchus skeleton.
facts.quote: Specimens of the turtle Kayentachelys, the dinosaur Scutellosaurus, and tritylodonts were found in the immediate vicinity a few meters below it.

facts.statement: The genus Kayentasuchus was formally named in 2002 by James M. Clark and Hans-Dieter Sues.
facts.quote: Kayentasuchus was named in 2002 by Clark and Hans-Dieter Sues.

facts.statement: The type species, K. walkeri, was named in honor of the paleontologist Alick Walker.
facts.quote: The type species is K. walkeri in memory of Alick Walker, a well-known paleontologist.

facts.statement: The teeth were nearly conical with distinct unserrated edges on both the front and back.
facts.quote: The teeth were nearly conical, but had distinct unserrated anterior and posterior edges.

facts.statement: The upper jaw tip held four teeth on each side, while the main jaw bones carried twelve or thirteen teeth each.
facts.quote: Each side of the tip of the upper jaw had four teeth, while the maxillae (main tooth-bearing bone of the upper jaw) and dentaries (tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw) had twelve or thirteen each.

facts.statement: The thigh bones were slender, and the animal had bony scutes covering both its back and belly.
facts.quote: The thigh bones were slender, and there were bony scutes on both the back and belly.

facts.statement: The scutes on the back were arranged in two rows that ran the full length of the animal.
facts.quote: The scutes on the upper surface were arranged in two rows running the length of the animal.

facts.statement: Kayentasuchus is a genus of sphenosuchian, a basal member of the crocodylomorph clade that includes crocodilians and their closest relatives.
facts.quote: Kayentasuchus (meaning "Kayenta Formation crocodile") is a genus of sphenosuchian, a type of basal crocodylomorph, the clade that comprises the crocodilians and their closest kin.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Kayentasuchus in an unresolved position among sphenosuchians, distinct from both true crocodiles and the genus Sphenosuchus.
facts.quote: Clark and Sues performed a phylogenetic analysis and found Kayentasuchus to have an unresolved position along with several other sphenosuchians, neither closer to true crocodiles or to Sphenosuchus.

facts.statement: Kayentasuchus lived between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago during the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Pliensbachian (199.5 to 184.2 million years ago)
